subject: Recap + next asks: deployment mode decision for BrightCart pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@brightcart.com>, Priya Sethi <priya@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next asks: deployment mode decision for BrightCart pilot

Thanks again for the demo earlier, Alex and Priya — good discussion. Quick recap from our side and a short list of clarifying questions so we can size the right pilot and recommend hosted vs dedicated (or private) for BrightCart.

What we heard on the call (please correct if anything is off):
- Primary use: product catalog search + recommendation enrichment on checkout flows.
- Typical request size: ~100–150 input tokens; responses average ~80 tokens.
- Current observed steady traffic: ~40 QPS, but spikes during campaigns/events up to ~220 QPS for short bursts.
- Target p95 latency for inference: ~<200ms for interactive checkout flows; less strict for background enrichment.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required; VPC/on-prem discussion later in procurement.

To validate assumption above and recommend the right deployment mode, could you confirm the following?
1) Expected steady-state QPS and expected peak burst duration (minutes).
2) p95 latency requirement: is 200ms a hard cutoff for checkout, or is 250ms acceptable with retries/fallbacks?
3) Token budget sensitivity: is per-token cost a primary constraint (i.e., would you trade 20% higher latency for 30% lower cost)?
4) Data residency/VPC needs for pilot: do you need a private VPC for the pilot or is hosted acceptable for the two-week evaluation?
5) Pilot window: are you aiming to start the pilot within two weeks?

Attachments: please share a traffic sample CSV if you can (sample shape we can run through our profiler). I attached a one-pager pilot checklist (attached in follow-up).

Next suggested step: short sync with Neha (solutions) and Marissa (CS) — copied — so we can propose a concrete pilot plan (config, SLOs, and cost ballpark). Would tomorrow or Thursday afternoon PST work for a 30-min call?

Thanks,

Thanks Ben — great notes. Confirming answers inline below.

On Tue, Jan 10, 2028 at 3:12 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> What we heard on the call (please correct if anything is off):

All accurate. A few specifics to add.

1) QPS: steady ~35–45 QPS (we expect growth). Peak bursts: ~200–260 QPS, typically 3–12 minutes during big campaigns.
2) p95 latency: checkout flow needs ~<=180ms ideally. We can tolerate up to 230ms with client-side fallback for up to 10% of requests.
3) Cost sensitivity: we want to keep cloud inference cost predictable; we'd prefer lower cost but not at the expense of breaking checkout. So latency takes priority for checkout. For background enrichment, cost trumps latency.
4) Pilot VPC: Hosted is okay for an initial two-week pilot (we need SOC2 evidence and an NDA amendment to include limited logs). If pilot meets latency, procurement will push for VPC for production.
5) Timeline: we can target a pilot start on Jan 24 (two weeks out).

Attaching a small traffic sample (CSV) that matches what we discussed. Let us know if you need a larger sample.

—Alex Johnson

Looping in Neha (solutions) and Marissa (CS) to propose a concrete pilot scope and initial sizing based on Alex's answers + the CSV.

Quick proposed approach from my side:
- Pilot objective: validate p95 <= 200ms for checkout at brightcart peak patterns; verify cost per 1k requests.
- Pilot duration: 2 weeks (production-like traffic using the attached sample, with one weekend load test to exercise peaks).
- Recommendation to validate: run a hosted API baseline for 48 hours to confirm feasibility. If hosted baseline is marginal, spin a short Dedicated reserved pool (2–4 GPUs depending on model) for a 10-day dedicated evaluation with auto-fallback to hosted.

Neha/Marissa — can you draft the pilot scope (config options, model variant, target SLOs, monitoring hooks, and a cost estimate)? I attached a pilot-scope doc and a draft SLA for reference. If we align, I'll schedule the Jan 24 kickoff and share the traffic Drive link with you.

Thanks Ben — reviewed Alex's CSV and the pilot scope. Short recommendation and next actions below.

Summary recommendation:
- Start with a 48-hour hosted baseline: this is low friction for BrightCart and will give us real latency numbers with their traffic shape. We will run with low-batching / single-token latency optimizations and no aggressive KV caching for the first run so we measure worst-case.
- If hosted baseline DOES NOT hit the p95 <= 200ms objective during simulated peak windows, we propose a 10-day Dedicated reserved pool pilot (2 x A100-class GPUs equivalent) configured with:
  - model variant: r-instruct-13B (quantized path)
  - autoscale: fixed headroom for expected peak + 30% burst buffer
  - batching: conservative (to preserve p95), with an option to enable throughput-mode during background enrichment endpoints
  - canary/fallback: traffic routed to hosted for 10% of requests for safety while evaluating dedicated pool
- Security: SOC2 evidence + NDA amendment for logs will be provided ahead of pilot start; if procurement requires VPC for production, we will run a parallel plan but not needed for this initial pilot.

Estimated effort & cost (very rough):
- Hosted baseline: <24 hours of SE time to profile + monitoring setup; infra cost ~small (pay as you go).
- Dedicated trial (if needed): setup & w/ops ~2 business days; estimated reserved cost ~USD 12k–18k for the 10-day trial depending on GPU class. We'll refine after we choose model and exact GPU SKU.

Next actions:
1) Alex/Priya: confirm Jan 24 kickoff (Ben to schedule).
2) Alex: grant Drive access to the traffic folder and share a second CSV with a two-hour peak window if possible.
3) Marissa: I suggest we add a brief runbook item for client-side fallback behavior if p95 exceeds 230ms for any sustained window.

I can prepare the dedicated pilot cost estimate and a short runbook by Monday (Jan 15) if you want to keep procurement timelines moving.

Available times for the Jan 24 kickoff: 9–11am PST or 1–3pm PST. Ben — if you want me on the kickoff, I can join the morning slot.
